content.text: You have the technology. You don't have a proposal team.
From "I could never write a federal proposal" to a submission-ready Word document.

RFP Pipeline is the guided, AI-accelerated, compliance-safe path a technical founder takes to a submitted federal proposal. We rank the opportunities worth your time, turn your own company documents into reusable content, and draft every section into an expert-built, compliance-bound template — so the money becomes reachable and the paperwork stops being the wall.
01 · Federal money is real. The paperwork was the obstacle — not the money.

Federal agencies fund early-stage R&D through SBIR, STTR, OTA, CSO, and BAA programs, and the funding is non-dilutive: you keep 100% of your equity and your IP — no investor, no board seat given up. The award is real cash for work you already want to do. The barrier has never been the money; it has been the proposal itself — hundreds of pages of rules, formatting, and volumes. That is the part RFP Pipeline removes.
Award ranges are public program figures and vary by agency and year — confirm the current number in each solicitation. Illustrative, not a quote.

content.text: Non-dilutive capital, on rails.

The proposal operating system for government-contracting SMBs and the EconDev organizations that back them. We turn the federal non-dilutive funding maze — SBIR, STTR, OTA, CSO, BAA — into a guided path: expert-curated opportunities, ranked to each company, and drafted by AI into compliance-ready proposals you download and submit.

content.text: The problem — a path problem, not a money problem

Billions in non-dilutive funding go unclaimed — not for lack of money, but for lack of a path. Program scale is public and defensible; the friction between a capable company and that capital is the opportunity.

items.text: Discovery is noise — thousands of solicitations across dozens of agencies and portals; the right one is a needle in a haystack, and deadlines pass unseen.
The blank page — even a strong company stalls at a blank Volume I: 20–50 pages of tightly-specified, compliance-bound technical writing.
Compliance is pass / fail — miss a required section, a page limit, or a format rule and a fundable idea is thrown out unread, before the science is ever evaluated.
Support doesn't scale — EconDev orgs, accelerators, and PTACs want whole portfolios of SMBs to win, but hand-holding each proposal one-by-one doesn't scale.

content.alt_text: Program-scale stat band: ~$4B+/yr, 11 agencies, $150K–$300K+ Phase I, 0% equity
content.caption: Public, defensible program scale

content.text: The solution & product — one spine, end to end

Curated → ranked → library → skeleton → AI-draft → download. Experts pre-build the skeleton so the customer never faces a blank page; AI drafts each section into a compliance-bound mold from the company's own learning library.

content.alt_text: Six-step product spine — Curate, Rank, Library, Skeleton, AI Draft, Review & Download — with a learning loop returning won content to the library
content.caption: The value spine plus the learning loop

items.text: Curate — RFP experts ingest federal solicitations into one live opportunity river.
Rank — each company gets a personalized feed via up to 5 Spotlight buckets; one card per opportunity, scored to their agency/tech/program lenses.
Library — upload company docs; we 'atomize' them into tagged, reusable content atoms (bios, past-performance blurbs, figures). The library learns.
Skeleton — experts pre-build each opportunity: a compliance matrix, a section outline, and canvas 'mold' templates per required document.
AI Draft — AI writes each section into the compliance-bound mold from the company's library plus the RFP context.

Review & Download — collaborate with stage-scoped roles (including an EconDev 'shadow' supporter), lock sections, and download a submission-ready Word document; a compliance matrix tracks completeness.

content.text: The moat: expert-curated skeletons & molds (not DIY search); a learning atom library that compounds every proposal (winning content returns as new atoms); and compliance baked in — tracked, not bolted on.
Market, wedge & business model

Land through EconDev; expand across every SBIR-seeking SMB. The go-to-market wedge: land one EconDev organization and reach its entire portfolio of small businesses. The stage-scoped 'shadow' role lets that org support every build — a force multiplier, not a single seat.

Why now, roadmap & the ask

The tailwinds just turned — and the spine is live. Why now: (1) AI can finally draft to spec — models can draft compliance-bound technical narrative into a fixed mold from a company's own library; (2) non-dilutive capital is in demand — founders wary of dilution favor grant capital that costs no equity; (3) government is digitizing — solicitations, portals, and submission are increasingly structured and can be systematized.
